title: Perfect scalar cohomology and two-term perfect models over principal ideal domains
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and use its module derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $P\in D(A)$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], then $H^q(P)$ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] for every $q\in\mathbf Z$, and vanishes outside the finite term interval of any bounded finite-projective representative. In addition, suppose $A$ is a principal ideal domain, meaning $1\ne0$, no zero divisors, and every ideal is generated by one element. For every finitely presented $A$-module $N$ and every specified surjection $v:A^r\to N$ with $r<\infty$, there are $s<\infty$ and an injective map $u:A^s\to A^r$ with $\operatorname{im}u=\ker v$, such that the augmentation
$$[A^s\xrightarrow{u}A^r]\longrightarrow N[0]$$
in degrees $[-1,0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $N[0]$ is perfect and lies in the thick subcategory generated by $A[0]$ [pur9-def-thick]. The module $N$ need not be torsion-free; zero modules and zero ranks are included.

source.place: Tag 0657 (definition-perfect), Tag 066Q (lemma-perfect-module), and Tag 0ATI (lemma-perfect-ring-classical-generator); Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.11(3), finite projective resolution paragraph. Noetherian cycles/quotients and PID freeness give the explicit scalar supplement.

proof.text: By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], choose a bounded complex $C^\bullet$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules representing $P$. Fix any term interval $[a,b]$ for this representative, so $C^q=0$ for $q<a$ or $q>b$. The cohomology functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $H^q(P)\cong H^q(C^\bullet)=Z^q/B^q$, with $Z^q=\ker(d^q:C^q\to C^{q+1})$ and $B^q=\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})\subseteq Z^q$ because $d^qd^{q-1}=0$. Outside $[a,b]$, the ambient module $C^q$ is zero, so $Z^q=B^q=0$ and $H^q(P)=0$. This works for each bounded finite-projective representative, not merely for the chosen one.

source.place: Tag 0657 (definition-perfect), bounded finite-projective representative; cohomology formula from derived.tex, Tag 05RU (definition-derived-category).

proof.text: For every $q$, the module $C^q$ is finitely generated. Since $A$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] applies to $Z^q\subseteq C^q$ and makes $Z^q$ finitely generated. If $z_1,\ldots,z_t$ generate $Z^q$, their images generate $Z^q/B^q$: a class represented by $z=\sum_j a_jz_j$ equals $\sum_j a_j[z_j]$. Thus $H^q(C^\bullet)$ is finitely generated. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation] to this module over the same Noetherian ring $A$. It is finitely presented, and the isomorphism of step 1 gives the assertion for $H^q(P)$: compose a finite presentation onto $H^q(C^\bullet)$ with that isomorphism; its kernel is unchanged.

source.place: Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), first and second assertions; Tag 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation), parts (1)-(2).

proof.text: Now assume that $A$ is a PID and retain the specified surjection $v:A^r\to N$. Set $S=\ker v\subseteq A^r$. The standard coordinate vectors form a finite basis of $A^r$: a tuple $x$ has the unique expansion $x=\sum_{j\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)}x_j e_j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pid-submodule-finite-basis] to obtain a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $S$, with $s\geq0$ finite. Define $h:A^s\to S$ by $h((a_i))=\sum_i a_i b_i$; uniqueness and existence of basis coordinates say exactly that $h$ is bijective and its inverse is linear. Let $u$ be $h$ followed by the inclusion $S\hookrightarrow A^r$. Both maps are injective, and $h$ is onto $S$, hence $u$ is injective and $\operatorname{im}u=S=\ker v$. In particular $vu=0$. This construction keeps $v$ itself and places no torsion-free assumption on $N$.

source.place: Tag 0ASU (lemma-split-off-free-part), part (1), finite-free submodule argument; exact finite-basis form in Mathlib Submodule.nonempty_basis_of_pid.

proof.text: Form $F^\bullet$ with $F^{-1}=A^s$, $F^0=A^r$, differential $d^{-1}=u$, and zero terms elsewhere. The maps $\varepsilon^0=v$ and $\varepsilon^q=0$ for $q\ne0$ define an augmentation $\varepsilon:F^\bullet\to N[0]$, since $vu=0$. Its degree $-1$ cohomology is $\ker u=0$. Its degree $0$ cohomology is $A^r/\operatorname{im}u$ and $H^0(\varepsilon)$ sends $[x]$ to $v(x)$. This map is onto because $v$ is onto; if $v(x)=0$, then $x\in\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$, so $[x]=0$ and the map is injective. In all other degrees both cohomology modules vanish. Thus $H^q(\varepsilon)$ is an isomorphism for every $q$, exactly the quasi-isomorphism criterion of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 066Q (lemma-perfect-module), proof of (2) implies (1), written out for the length-one resolution; derived.tex Tag 05RU (definition-derived-category).

proof.text: The coordinate vectors give finite bases of $A^s$ and $A^r$, and the zero terms have the empty basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. In particular every term of $F^\bullet$ is finitely generated, and [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective] makes every term projective. The complex is bounded in $[-1,0]$, and step 4 identifies its image in $D(A)$ with $N[0]$. By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], $N[0]$ is perfect. Empty coordinate sets are allowed throughout, so the same reasoning includes $N=0$, $r=0$ or $s=0$ whenever the given surjection permits them.

source.place: Tag 0657 (definition-perfect) and Tag 066Q (lemma-perfect-module), proof of (2) implies (1); free modules are projective by algebra.tex Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-perfect-ring-classical-generator] over the commutative ring $A$. Its statement identifies the perfect objects of $D(A)$ with the thick subcategory generated by $A[0]$, including closure under isomorphisms and direct summands. The perfect object $N[0]$ from step 5 therefore belongs to that thick subcategory, as required.

proof_origin.place: Explicit scalar supplement combining Tags 0657, 066Q and 0ATI with algebra.tex Tags 00IK/00FP and more-algebra.tex Tag 0ASU. Motivated by Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 6.8.11(3), proof paragraph on a finite projective resolution of the scalar module.
